column1: # The corpus census: every file in this directory that carries pinned
# bytes, and whether those bytes have a lifecycle at all.
# THIS IS THE STABLE / REFRESHED SEPARATION, written down. The two are
# operationally different in a way no reader can infer from the files:
# a standards document's test vectors are frozen and a difference from
# the publisher is a defect in the pin, while vendor collateral is
# REISSUED on the vendor's own schedule and a difference is the pin
# needing refreshing. Treating them alike produces either a monitor that
# cries wolf every month or one that never notices a corrupted vector.
# COMPLETENESS IS MECHANICAL, and that is the point of the file.
# `t_attestation_fixture_lifecycle` scans this directory and requires a
# row for every file that matches any of:
#   * a run of twelve or more consecutive lines of sixty-plus
#     hexadecimal characters — a corpus, as opposed to the single digest
# A new corpus that matches none of those is not covered, and one row
# below is there because of exactly that: the malformed-CBOR corpus is
# RFC text with no hex and a name the rule does not match. It is listed
# by hand. Every row must name a file that exists, so a hand-added row
# cannot drift into fiction even though the scan did not find it.
